teaser: How to copy a working agentic email setup in phases: a mailbox and Claude seat of the agent's own, one session with a policy, then roles talking in files.
core_idea: Claude is used as an agent state machine, one session per role, every message between agents a file in a vault and every outgoing email a draft a person sends; the phases take you from one session to a team without ever breaking that rule.

nodes.label: Claude as a state machine
nodes.summary: Each role is one session that reads its state from a vault, does one kind of work, writes files back and stops.

nodes.label: Accounts of the agent's own
nodes.summary: A Workspace mailbox on a domain you own, a Claude Team seat, a GitHub account on the same identity; never your own inbox.

nodes.label: Connectors enabled, then connected
nodes.summary: On a Team plan the owner enables connectors for the organisation; the agent's own account then connects, so the OAuth grants live only there.

nodes.label: Calendar shared read-only
nodes.summary: The person's calendar is shared to the agent's account with read access, so it knows what is going on without being able to move anything.

nodes.label: The inbox agent
nodes.summary: The one session that reads the mailbox, labels, moves, summarises and writes replies to Drafts.

nodes.label: Policy before the first run
nodes.summary: Reach, mandate, gap and barriers written before the agent runs, even when there is only one agent.

nodes.label: Roles: inbox, writer, CRM, dev team
nodes.summary: Each role a session with a policy short enough to check; the policies share the reach and differ in the mandate.

nodes.label: Email-FS lite
nodes.summary: An inbox per agent as a folder in a vault; a message is a file with typed blocks, a reply is another file, and the vault keeps every version.

nodes.label: The agent drafts, a person sends
nodes.summary: Nothing is sent by an agent; everything lands in Drafts and the person reads, edits and presses send.

nodes.label: The security exception
nodes.summary: The one message that goes out without waiting is written into the policy as a named exception rather than left as a habit.

nodes.label: Interfaces for the moment
nodes.summary: Cards, drop zones and boards built by agents in an afternoon because the data was already files in a vault; each one gets a policy.

nodes.label: The record
nodes.summary: Every message a file, every draft in the mailbox, every decision a row: a footprint that can be read afterwards without touching anything.

nodes.label: Trust built from the record
nodes.summary: You do not have to believe what the agent says it did; you can read what it did, and give it more as the drafts you did not change pile up.

nodes.label: Schedules come later
nodes.summary: Running the sessions on a schedule is where this ends up, but start with sessions you open yourself; the schedule gets its own article.

quotes.text: Nothing is sent by an agent.
quotes.why: The rule that never changes, and the reason the setup gives the person more control rather than less.

quotes.text: You do not have to believe what the agent says it did. You can read what it did.
quotes.why: Why the record is the point for someone learning to trust a set of agents.
